clue.text: Bypass — is speed limit finally reduced?

indicators.note: reduced in the sense of broken down into pieces, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word limit only

parts.note: the last letter of limit

explanation.surface: A driver on a bypass wonders whether the speed limit has at last been lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep something is to avoid or go round it, just as a road bypasses a town.

clue.text: Pharmacist stocking drug gets stars

definitions.note: Bootes is the name of one constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: stocking means keeping goods on the shelves, so the pharmacist holds the drug inside

parts.note: Boots is the big British high-street chemist chain
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A chemist who keeps drugs in stock is rewarded with gold stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Pharmacist suggests a person, but it stands for the British high-street chemist chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootes, the Herdsman, is a northern constellation whose brightest member is Arcturus.

clue.text: Rascal observed penning pages about gangster

indicators.note: penning means shutting something in a pen, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: observed means seen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pages go round the gangster

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Someone spotted writing up a gangster's story in their notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two enclosures here: the pages wrap the gangster, and that pair then sits inside observed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spalpeen is an Irish word for a scamp or good-for-nothing, a rascal.

clue.text: Element of hospital meal, mostly very dry, eaten by tramp?

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: bum is slang for a tramp or vagrant

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: arid means very dry

explanation.surface: A tramp eating a dry, unappetising hospital dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A barium meal is a chalky liquid drunk before an X-ray so the gut shows up; the definition takes in the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Barium is the chemical element in the chalky drink patients swallow before certain X-rays.

clue.text: Maybe like a microphone trick to smother insolence

indicators.note: to smother is to cover completely, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
lip is cheeky talk, insolence

explanation.surface: A trick for silencing a cheeky speaker by muffling the microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Small lapel microphones attach by a clip, so they are described as clip-on.

clue.text: Brainboxes managed to penetrate spy agency

indicators.note: to penetrate is to get inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: the American intelligence agency
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Clever people have infiltrated an intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: Brainboxes reads as clever people, but here it means the bony boxes that hold brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Crania are skulls, literally the boxes in which brains are kept.

clue.text: Cut around soft spot

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the cut goes on either side

parts.note: to slash is to cut
p is piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: Cutting around a tender spot, as a surgeon might.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a small patch or dab of colour, as in a splash of paint.

clue.text: Troubles in hotel with relatives

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
aunts are relatives

explanation.surface: Family rows breaking out while staying in a hotel with relations.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone is to trouble or disturb them persistently, as a memory or ghost does.

clue.text: Silence poet conjured up in a time long ago

indicators.note: something conjured up is made by magic, so the letters are produced in a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiet poet summoned up from the distant past.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pleistocene is the geological epoch of the Ice Ages, ending about twelve thousand years back.

clue.text: Keen officer hugging ace soldiers

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping arms round, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
A is the ace in cards
soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: An officer embracing his finest troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Keen looks like an adjective meaning eager, but it is the verb meaning to wail for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, so as a noun a keen is a mournful cry or lament.

clue.text: Place where you'll find people who are little and large — bad place for one to be in

definitions.text: Place where you'll find people who are little

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

indicators.note: to be in means placed inside, so one goes between the other pieces

parts.note: ill means bad, and to put is to place
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Little and Large were a British comedy double act; the clue seems to joke about a poor venue for one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stops at little; large reads as half of the comedy duo but only supplies its abbreviation. One sits between bad and place.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliput is the island in Gulliver's Travels whose inhabitants are only a few inches tall.

clue.text: 'Moneymaker' that may grow in the garden

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the place where coins are struck

definitions.text: that may grow in the garden

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint that moneymaker is to be taken literally, a maker of money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the official coin factory and a common culinary herb grown in gardens.

clue.text: I'm dire pest to be given spray?

definitions.text: I'm dire pest to be given spray?

indicators.note: something given a spray is scattered about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden pest confesses it is awful and deserves to be sprayed with insecticide.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the creature speaking is a pest that gardeners spray.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider mites are tiny sap-sucking arachnids that infest plants and are controlled with insecticidal sprays.

clue.text: Fitting a number into sheltered accommodation to the east of a very quiet old city

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other
in an across clue east is to the right, so this part follows the earlier pieces

parts.note: taken as written
pp is pianissimo, very quiet in music
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
a tent is a shelter you sleep in
a as written, plus N for number

explanation.surface: Fitting another resident into a care home somewhere in an ancient, hushed city.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheltered accommodation suggests housing for the elderly, but it is simply a canvas shelter on a campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: Appurtenant means belonging or pertaining to something, hence fitting or appropriate to it.

clue.text: Act of sports official — superior male with holy anger

parts.note: U means upper class, superior
M is the abbreviation for male
pi is informal for pious, holy
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A haughty man berating the referee with righteous fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Holy anger looks like a single phrase, righteous wrath, but its two words are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpirage is the action or decision of an umpire, the official who adjudicates a game.

clue.text: Religious type with extreme characters in an uplifting ceremony

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up means reading from bottom to top
in means placed inside, so these characters go within the next word

parts.note: taken as written
Z and A are the letters at either end of the alphabet
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A devout person attending an inspiring religious service with some eccentric folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Extreme characters sounds like odd people; it means the letters at either end of the alphabet. The reversal applies to everything before ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nazarite was an ancient Israelite who took a vow of abstinence, so a religious devotee.

clue.text: Old coins found in grain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old English silver fourpenny pieces
second meaning: hulled cereal kernels such as oats

explanation.surface: Ancient coins unearthed in a sack of cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fourpenny coin of old England and also hulled, crushed cereal kernels.

clue.text: Snobbish as pig away from home apparently!

parts.note: the pig only says whose home is meant; it gives no letters

indicators.note: apparently tells the solver to take the picture literally, a pig not in its home

parts.note: a pig's home is a sty
away from home means not at home

explanation.surface: A haughty person is compared to a pig that has strayed from its pen.
explanation.walkthrough: A pig away from home is NOT in its STY, so NOT goes into STY: S(NOT)TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Snotty is an informal word for arrogant or condescending, looking down on others.

clue.text: Creep is dodgy when capturing photo? Don't step too close to these!

definitions.text: Don't step too close to these!
definitions.note: the definition is a warning sentence rather than a plain noun

indicators.note: capturing means taking hold of, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
pic is short for picture, a photo

explanation.surface: A sneaky photographer leaning out over a cliff edge for a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: CREEP IS is jumbled to PRECIES, which then holds PIC: PRECI(PIC)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipices are sheer cliff faces, places where stepping near the edge risks a fall.

clue.text: Club characters regularly coming in could get on well together

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of could
people who gel get on well together

explanation.surface: Members of a club who drift in regularly might find they get along.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short heavy stick used as a weapon, in other words a club.

clue.text: The old man's upset, a soldier

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that reads bottom to top

parts.note: pa is the old man, father, plus the possessive s
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: Father is distressed because he is a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A sapper is a military engineer, a soldier who digs trenches and tunnels.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapper is the term for a combat engineer, a private soldier of the Royal Engineers.

clue.text: Sound asleep, having abandoned party

indicators.note: having abandoned means having left behind, so the named part is removed

parts.note: dozing means lightly asleep
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Fast asleep after leaving the party early.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound asleep reads as one phrase meaning deeply asleep, but sound is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A zing is a sharp high-pitched whine, the sound of something speeding past.

clue.text: Fellow introducing singer Bobby is a bigwig

indicators.note: introducing means going before, so this piece leads the next

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Bobby Darin, the American singer of Mack the Knife

explanation.surface: A compere introducing Bobby Darin on stage is someone important.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a powerful official, especially a senior civil servant, a bigwig.

clue.text: Correspondence from one in political organisation

indicators.note: in means inside, so one goes within the organisation

parts.note: a political party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A letter from a member of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Correspondence suggests letters, but here it means a matching or equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality or close correspondence between things, as between two currencies.

clue.text: Reportedly top vehicle for winter conditions

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or heard, so the word is judged by its pronunciation

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them, to slay

explanation.surface: News of the best car to drive in snowy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Top looks like an adjective meaning best, but it is the slang verb to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn over snow by horses or reindeer, a winter vehicle.

clue.text: Uncultivated, like a Ted of yesteryear?

parts.note: Ted Heath, British Prime Minister in the early 1970s
the suffix -y turns a noun into an adjective meaning like it

explanation.surface: Asking whether something resembles a figure from the past called Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath, known as Ted, was the British Conservative Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathy describes land covered in heath, wild open ground left uncultivated.
